items.title: [abcnews.com] Trump replaces national cyber director after outages disrupt US services
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

President Donald Trump replaced National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross with Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies as acting director after a week of outages disrupted aviation, banking, communications and government systems. The incidents have drawn scrutiny of the administration’s response, although officials say there is no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack or a connection among the failures. A source familiar with the White House’s thinking said Trump supported Cairncross’s removal because he lacked strong cybersecurity credentials. Trump said Friday, “I didn’t think that person was good enough”. Axios reported that Chief of Staff Stephen Miller pushed for the change on similar grounds. Cairncross, a former Republican National Committee executive, said he was proud of his work in the role. Davies has held cybersecurity and technology leadership jobs at Unilever, Estée Lauder, Barclays-Africa Group, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Siemens. Davies will serve temporarily. A permanent director must be nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate, which Democrats are due to control in January. Cybersecurity experts say companies’ rapid efforts to patch software vulnerabilities may be behind some disruptions, as advanced AI tools make those flaws easier to find.

The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approved construction permits on Nov. 9 for four advanced reactors at Dow’s Seadrift chemical complex on the Texas Gulf Coast, a project developed with reactor company X-energy. The units are intended to provide electricity and process heat to the site. items.title: [space.com] Apollo 12 lightning strikes prompted NASA to tighten launch weather rules
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Lightning struck NASA’s Apollo 12 Saturn V rocket twice within seconds of its Nov. 14, 1969, launch, disrupting spacecraft telemetry and endangering the mission. Mission Control engineer John Aaron recognized the readings from an earlier test and recommended switching the Signal Conditioning Equipment to its auxiliary setting, which restored the data. Investigators concluded the rocket and its conductive exhaust plume had triggered a discharge in an electrically charged part of the atmosphere, even though no active thunderstorm lay along the immediate flight path. NASA expanded launch weather restrictions to account for atmospheric electrical conditions, not only visible lightning and thunderstorms.

items.title: [scmp.com] Trump threatens tax on U.S. tech firms building AI data centres abroad
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

President Donald Trump threatened a “tremendous tax” on U.S. technology companies that build artificial-intelligence data centres overseas, saying the facilities should remain in the United States to prevent China from gaining access to computing capacity. He gave no details on the proposed penalty and said he had not discussed it with his administration, leaving unclear how it could be imposed. Trump urged communities to accept domestic projects and negotiate payments or other benefits from developers. About three-quarters of U.S. voters opposed building a data centre in their community, with residents citing electricity prices and water use as concerns. The administration is tightening restrictions on remote access to advanced U.S. chips and servers to prevent Chinese firms from using computing capacity hosted in third countries. Technology companies are offering communities more transparency, environmental commitments and financial contributions to secure approval for projects.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Alberta bill sets data-centre limits and well cleanup funds
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Alberta introduced Bill 42 on Nov. 18, proposing new siting and water rules for large data centres and mandatory cleanup funding for every new oil and gas well. Centres using at least 10 megawatts would generally have to be at least 600 metres from homes and avoid top-quality or irrigated farmland; they would also face a near-zero cooling-water standard. The Alberta Utilities Commission would regulate the larger facilities. The province says about 30% of current proposals could be affected, while projects already far along in approvals or construction would be exempt. For new wells, companies would pay up to $50,000 initially and make equal annual payments for up to 10 years. The money would remain attached to the well if ownership changes. If a well becomes orphaned, its funding would go to the Orphan Well Association. The requirements are expected to cover wells drilled after April 1, 2027. The bill would also eliminate Alberta’s oil-sands emissions cap, which the province says is redundant with industrial carbon pricing.

items.title: [kyivindependent.com] Regulators warn Russian grid strikes put Ukraine’s reactors at risk
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

International nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries warned on Nov. 16 that attacks on Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure are increasing the risk of a nuclear accident this winter. The three groups behind the statement—the Western European Nuclear Regulators Association, the Heads of European Radiological Protection Competent Authorities and the Heads of Nordic Radiation Safety Authorities—called on Russia to stop attacks on nuclear facilities and the power network needed to operate them safely. Ukraine’s three operating nuclear plants have nine generating reactors and supply about 80% of the country’s electricity this winter. The plants also need a stable power supply to run cooling and other safety systems. The International Atomic Energy Agency said military activity disrupted the grid in the week before Nov. 14, forcing some units to reduce output. The Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant is not generating electricity but needs external power to cool its nuclear material. It has lost off-site power 27 times since the war began and has relied on one external line since late March. Per Strand, who heads two of the regulatory groups, warned that a nationwide blackout could affect all nine operating reactors simultaneously and urged European countries to coordinate emergency preparations if attacks continue. International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi has called for an end to military operations against electricity infrastructure linked to nuclear safety and urged both sides to keep working with the agency.

items.title: [japantimes.co.jp] Climate change intensified Indonesia’s worst wildfires in a decade, study finds
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

A World Weather Attribution study published Friday found that a strong El Niño drove Indonesia’s severe rainfall shortfall this year, while human-caused climate change made temperatures during the August-to-October fire season about 1.6 degrees Celsius higher. Researchers said warming made hot, dry fire conditions about three times more likely, while El Niño cut seasonal rainfall by roughly half. Decades of deforestation and peatland drainage also left the landscape more vulnerable to ignition. The fires have spread hazardous haze across Indonesia and neighboring Southeast Asian countries. Nusantara Atlas, an independent monitoring platform, estimated that fires affected 2.88 million hectares from January through October. The Indonesian government had not confirmed that total or issued its own estimate. Researchers called for peatland restoration, stronger land protections and reduced fossil-fuel emissions. Fires were still burning, with smoke detected in eastern Kalimantan on Nov. 12.

items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

MIT researchers found that older adults had significantly weaker waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which helps clear waste from the brain during sleep, than younger adults. The researchers used brain imaging and electroencephalography to study volunteers ages 18 to 39 and 60 to 84, linking the reduced flow partly to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and diminished vascular responses. Separately, a study described in a paper shared on Reddit found that LSD-related gene-expression patterns in rats and mice ran counter to some patterns associated with human brain aging. LSD also reduced certain amyloid-beta-related changes in mouse brain-cell cultures. These are preclinical findings, not evidence that LSD prevents dementia in people.

items.title: [nation.com.pk] WHO warns rising drug resistance is eroding last-line antibiotic options
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Drug-resistant bacterial infections are increasing across regions. The World Health Organization and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control report that European Klebsiella pneumoniae infections rose 72% from 2019 to 2025, while resistance in monitored E. coli infections also increased. Globally, one in six laboratory-confirmed common bacterial infections was resistant to antibiotics in 2023, according to the WHO. When standard antibiotics fail, clinicians may turn to carbapenems, but resistance to these last-line drugs is also rising. In the Americas, carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae increased from about 15% in 2015 to 26% in 2024; median resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii was 77% across the seven reporting countries. Health authorities are calling for stronger infection prevention, laboratory diagnosis and surveillance; the Pan American Health Organization’s 2027–2031 action plan was approved in September.
